messages:
matt: Heads-up — saw a reproducible p99 latency bump on a dedicated pool during a sustained long-context workload. Looks tied to KV pager activity + eviction thrash when load spikes. Sharing traces and a short log excerpt.

jana: Curious, is this LRU or FIFO path? we've been toggling heuristics in the canary.

matt: Repro uses LRU in prod, but when we fallback to FIFO under heavy pressure it gets worse. Stack: runtime->kv-pager->evicter. Sample logs: 
```
[2026-02-14T14:22:01Z] pager: request id=abc123 seq_len=8192 kv_size=2.1GiB
[2026-02-14T14:22:01Z] pager: evicting batch=512 reclaimed=1 reused=3 frag=0.31
[2026-02-14T14:22:01Z] runtime: p99=163ms p50=12ms token_rate=420/s
[2026-02-14T14:22:01Z] pager: eviction-loop duration=98ms stall=true
```

jana: that frag number (0.31) is high for the allocator pattern — might be slab boundary churn. Did you capture kv timestamps for reinsert ordering?

matt: yes, i dumped a tiny repro trace — looks like reinserts reorder relative to eviction markers and at high concurrency we hit a correctness probe that causes synchronous disk/page scans. snippet of the repro (python):
```
# repro: hammer pool with long seeds
for _ in range(3000):
    client.generate(prompt=long_prompt, max_tokens=4096)
```

oliver: could be interaction between batching heuristics and kernel selection. If kernels take longer for long sequences (we've seen a ~2x latency on the new attention kernel), batching backs up requests and keeps KV entries hot longer which increases pager pressure.

maria: i ran a kernel perf comparison yesterday — the new fused-attn path saves cycles at mid lengths but regresses at >6k due to memory layout. i'll post numbers later, but that matches your observation.

dave: what about correctness — are we losing entries or just stalling? any invariant violations flagged?

matt: no invariants broken per stack asserts, but we do see an evicter loop that switches from async reclaim to sync fallback when reclaimers fall behind. that fallback causes the big latency spike.

perf-bot: CI flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.internal/flames/1798765433 (permission: eng-runtime) :eyes:

jana: quick mitigation idea: cap batch size when seq_len distribution tail > 90th pct, and add a pacing token to eviction so we never fall into immediate sync fallback. small config example: 
```
kv.eviction.max_batch = 256
kv.eviction.throttle_ms = 20
kv.reuse.ttl_ms = 300000
```

oliver: other quick win: make FIFO/LRU tie-breaker stable via monotonic insert counters so reinserts don't end up ahead of older entries. that should remove reorder-caused sync scans. low-risk patch.

maria: i'll run canary with both kernel rollback and the stable-tie-breaker on a subset of the pool. if canary looks ok we can push a flip.

dave: can you also add a lightweight sampler to record "evict->reinsert latency" for entries? that'll give us a signal to alert before full sync fallback.

matt: good call. i'll add a per-pool metric: evict_reinsert_ms p95 and hook it into console dashboards + perf alerts.

jana: for the long term we should think about fragmentation-aware eviction that prefers contiguous slab ranges. that'll help with the frag=0.31 cases.

oliver: agree. short term: stable tie-breaker + throttle + batch cap + p95 metric. i'll open a PR for the tie-breaker.
maria: canary started at 14:40 PT on pool-12 with kernel=stable and eviction.patch=stable-tiebreaker. i'll ping once we hit 1h and 6h marks.
matt: thanks team. if anyone wants the repro runs i have a script and a small dataset (will attach). :thumbsup:

dave: i'll rerun a couple of long-context L7 requests against canary and post traces. :rocket:
